# TARGET_CONTRACTS — Sylius 2.3 API arm

Common reviewed declaration and behavior supplement for both checked-interface hidden views.

Upstream source: `70cf6ca686ec3efa4635a451bdd2b1358ab71d42`.
Current readable projection: `source_files_digest 85ee08d44e42ae299ae6ce03da46c76c1255914a8a6c9b0eb0a5cfd6c71d8d76`; `runtime_seed_digest 4684969ad20842711c1d8a4150f3d8b1d195ae9eee597739663cc8313ced098a`; 11073 files; collection tag `sylius-checked-interfaces-v2-collection-20260920`. The runtime refresh changes only the recorder.

The reviewed API text below is preserved from `onb-sprint-3-sylius`. Its selection-count and review-history notes describe the historical maps/samples, not this 319-implementation census. Current eligibility is 666 of 1,950 requirements, with 1,284 reviewed exclusions. The current map selects only eligible entries; historical fallback targets are not used.

This supplement covers **the 160 declarations in 102 classes that the final map
hides**, and nothing else. 159 of those declarations in 101 classes are hidden on
a target-bearing requirement; the 160th, `MessengerPersistProcessor::process`, is
hidden only as the labelled fallback of the 1,277 excluded items (§16). It replaces the DRAFT scaffold carried from
`maps/sylius/TARGET_CONTRACTS.md` at `c7f91589`, which was written for the draft
map's principal set.

No declaration below promises inherited framework defaults unless explicitly cited.

## How to read an entry

Each class gets its declaration line and its registration (service id, registry
tag, API Platform operation, or Doctrine resource entry), then one entry per
hidden body:

* the **full signature** as declared — visibility, `static`/`final`, name, typed
  parameters with defaults, return type — with the body's line span;
* the **interface or abstract method it implements**, with that declaration's own
  docblock where it has one;
* the declaration's **own docblock**;
* the **exceptions** it declares (`@throws`) or constructs (`throw new`);
* one **behavioural contract** sentence, written from the requirements that select
  the body and from its callers. Every clause names its source in italics.

A contract sentence says what a caller may rely on. It deliberately does **not**
say how the body computes it: a reader with only this file can write a test that
pins the behaviour, and cannot reconstruct the implementation. Where the only
honest statement is the declaration itself, the entry says **signature only** and
gives the reason — for a private helper whose sole caller is another hidden body,
no caller-observable contract exists to state.

Two source labels need a word:

* *(requirement `sylius/features/...:N`)* cites a release item whose gold coverage
  selects this body; the item id is checked against the map's own selection for
  that declaration, so a citation here is never decorative.
* *(caller `src/...php:N`)* cites a first-party call site in a file that imports
  the declaring class or one of its interfaces. Call sites in `tests/` and in
  same-named methods of unrelated classes are excluded.

## What this supplement does not promise

* It does not describe the 1,277 items the ruling excludes from the level-2
  sample; those items hide only the labelled fallback principal
  (`MessengerPersistProcessor::process`, §16).
* It does not restate the readable source. Constructors, class constants,
  interfaces, DTO commands, constraint classes, form types and service
  configuration all stay visible in every view; where a contract fact lives in
  one of them, this file cites it rather than copying it.
* It makes no claim about Symfony, Doctrine, API Platform or Webmozart
  behaviour beyond the signatures Sylius declares against them.
* Under `all_hidden` the view replaces **every** production body, not only these 160.

Feature: Receiving a welcoming email after registration
    In order to receive proof that my account has been created
    As a Visitor
    I want to receive the welcoming email

    Background:
        Given the store operates on a single channel in "United States"
        And that channel allows to shop using "English (United States)" and "Polish (Poland)" locales

    @api @ui @email
    Scenario: Receiving a welcoming email after registration when channel has disabled registration verification
        Given on this channel account verification is not required
        When I register with email "ghastly@bespoke.com" and password "suitsarelife"
        Then only one email should have been sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com"
        And a welcoming email should have been sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com"

    @api @ui @email
    Scenario: Receiving an account verification email after registration when channel has enabled registration verification
        Given on this channel account verification is required
        When I register with email "ghastly@bespoke.com" and password "suitsarelife"
        Then only one email should have been sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com"
        And a verification email should have been sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com"
        But a welcoming email should not have been sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com"

    @api @ui @email
    Scenario: Receiving a welcoming email after registration in different locale than the default one
        Given on this channel account verification is not required
        When I register with email "ghastly@bespoke.com" and password "suitsarelife" in the "Polish (Poland)" locale
        Then a welcoming email should have been sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com" in "Polish (Poland)" locale

    @api @ui @email
    Scenario: Receiving a welcoming email after account verification when channel has enabled registration verification
        Given on this channel account verification is required
        And I register with email "ghastly@bespoke.com" and password "suitsarelife"
        When I verify my account using link sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com"
        Then a welcoming email should have been sent to "ghastly@bespoke.com"
